A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoP work. Their text, figures, tables, algorithms, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison: Appendices A-M in v1 and A-Q in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original CoP jailbreak experiments, attack-success rates, query counts, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original guarded-target, JailbreakBench, X-Teaming, component-ablation, and fluency results.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix C retain the same seed generation, seven principles, composition procedure, dual judging, and iterative refinement. CoP remains single-turn; the new ablations test existing components.

E1.justification: V2 adds JailbreakBench's 100 harmful queries and a Llama-2-7B-Chat deployment protected by Llama-Guard-3 input/output filtering. Section 4.4 also evaluates conversational X-Teaming attacks, extending interaction conditions while retaining single-turn CoP. These substantially broaden benchmark and test-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: X-Teaming moves from related-work discussion to an evaluated comparator in Table 3. Existing baseline suites are otherwise retained. Figure 3 also newly plots AutoDAN-Turbo against O1 and Claude, but Section 4.1 still says these comparisons were omitted, leaving their actual participation inconsistent.

E3.justification: New protocols include X-Teaming turn limits from one to five on 50 HarmBench queries, a 100-query JailbreakBench comparison with 20 iterations, and additional controlled component/judge tests on 50 queries. Average perplexity is introduced for fluency evaluation. The original Appendix C settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds GPT-3.5 versus GPT-4 judging, seed-removal and single-principle ablations, external-guard robustness testing, and fluency analysis with an additional attack trace. Table 10 newly reports 72% ASR without seed generation and 30% with single-principle selection, versus 88% full CoP. Its similarity-judge comparison already appeared in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and the existing query-time boxplots are retained; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New results include 34% CoP ASR with Llama-Guard-3, 81% on JailbreakBench, component/judge and X-Teaming comparisons, and perplexity 14.054. O1/Claude query counts disappear from Table 1. V2 Figure 3 corrects several AutoDAN-Turbo bars toward unchanged appendix-table values, including approximately 42.6% to 47.2% on Llama-2-70B. It also introduces O1/Claude bars of 10%/12%, contradicting the stated exclusion. These are reported-result changes, not demonstrated same-setting CoP improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical notation, jailbreak definitions, thresholds, and algorithmic reasoning are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introduction contributions retain the same effectiveness, transparency, up-to-19-times ASR improvement, and up-to-17.2-times query-reduction claims. The conclusion changes its commercial-model examples to O1 and Claude, which were already evaluated in v1.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new composition ablations, single-turn versus conversational comparison, and fluency results, and acknowledges imperfect automated-judge precision in Appendix K. It removes v1's circuit-breaker-specific mechanism explanation and discussion of Claude's success-versus-query-cost tradeoff. The central interpretation of CoP remains intact.

D1.justification: New sections provide limited setup details, including Llama-Guard-3 filtering both inputs and outputs and JailbreakBench's 20-iteration budget with HarmBench classification. Appendix C's implementation, templates, default models, thresholds, and hardware information are unchanged. The identical project URL moves to a footnote.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a substantive comparison with GPTFuzzer, distinguishing query-specific design, multi-principle composition, and dual evaluation. Existing related-work discussions and the numbered bibliography remain largely unchanged. New GPTFuzzer, JailbreakBench, and guard references contain unresolved citation markers.

P1.justification: V2 moves the strategy-frequency discussion from Section 4.3 to Appendix I and relocates the original qualitative example section. It rewrites selected evaluation and related-work passages and adds a funding statement. Most existing prose, including the abstract and method explanation, is retained.

P2.justification: V2 separates and redraws Figure 1(d) as Figure 2, redesigns the main ASR chart, and moves the strategy-frequency figure into the appendix. It contracts Table 1, expands Table 2, and adds comparison, ablation, and fluency tables. Figure 8 supplies a new trace; Figures 7 and 9 both reproduce v1's Figure 4 image.

improvement.justification: The new composition/seed controls and additional benchmark and guarded-target tests strengthen validation. However, v2 removes O1/Claude efficiency evidence and introduces AutoDAN-Turbo bars contradicting Section 4.1 and Figure 2's 2% best Claude baseline. This leaves the retained 19-times headline claim unreconciled. The PDFs do not resolve those comparisons, so the validation gains and weakened result consistency do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
